title: An interpretable machine learning model using SHapley Additive exPlanations for preoperative cervical lymph node metastasis risk stratification in tongue squamous cell carcinoma: a multicenter study.
summary: A logistic-regression radiomics model used preoperative MRI tumor-shape features and SHAP explanations to predict cervical lymph-node metastasis in 293 tongue-squamous-cell-carcinoma patients from two hospitals.
ai_technology: Methods identify the learned operation and data for the assigned case-specific result: A multicenter radiomics model predicted cervical lymph-node metastasis in tongue squamous-cell carcinoma patients.

evidence.tested: AUC was 0.818 in training, 0.739 in validation and 0.755 in testing; T2WI SurfaceVolumeRatio was the leading SHAP feature and clinical variables did not significantly improve performance. This retrospective multicenter evaluation does not show prospective treatment benefit.
evidence.unknown: The reviewed source does not establish prospective benefit, broad external validity, or replication beyond the reported study.
evidence.ai_role: A multicenter radiomics model predicted cervical lymph-node metastasis in tongue squamous-cell carcinoma patients.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
